Symptom.name: Robot controller not responding
Symptom.description: Robot controller not responding.

Symptom.name: All LEDs are OFF at Controller
Symptom.description: No LEDs at all are lit on the Control Module or the Drive Module respectively.

Symptom.name: No voltage in service outlet
Symptom.description: No voltage is available in the Control Module service outlet for powering external service equipment.

Symptom.name: Erratic event messages on FlexPendant
Symptom.description: The event messages displayed on the FlexPendant are erratic and do not seem to correspond to any actual malfunctions on the robot. Several types of messages can be displayed, seemingly erroneously.

Symptom.name: Problem jogging the robot
Symptom.description: The robot cannot be jogged properly.

Symptom.name: Inconsistent path accuracy
Symptom.description: The path of the robot TCP is not consistent. It varies from time to time, and is sometimes accompanied by noise emerging from bearings, gearboxes, or other locations.

Symptom.name: Oil and grease stains on motors and gearboxes
Symptom.description: The area surrounding the motor or gearbox shows signs of oil leaks. This can be at the base, closest to the mating surface, or at the furthest end of the motor at the resolver.

Symptom.name: Intermittent errors during operation
Symptom.description: Errors and malfunctions occur in a seemingly random way during operation.

Symptom.name: holding brakes non-operational
Symptom.description: Robot axes' holding brakes are disconnected, faulty, worn, or rendered non-operational.

Symptom.name: live voltage inside Drive Module
Symptom.description: Live voltage is accessible behind the rear covers and inside the front cover even when the main switches have been switched off.

Symptom.name: unit sensitive to ESD
Symptom.description: Sensitive electronics may be destroyed by electrostatic discharge during handling.

Symptom.name: hot parts may cause burns
Symptom.description: Manipulator parts and cabinet drive parts become hot and may cause burns.

Symptom.name: gearbox on axis 6 is getting hot
Symptom.description: Observation that the gearbox on axis 6 is getting hot.

Symptom.name: Controller cannot be started
Symptom.description: The system cannot be started. The joystick on the FlexPendant does not work.

Symptom.name: erratic robot behavior
Symptom.description: Robot behavior becomes erratic.

Symptom.name: problem starting the system
Symptom.description: Problem starting the system during start-up.

Symptom.name: LEDs not lit on any unit
Symptom.description: LEDs are not lit on any unit during start-up failure.

Symptom.name: earth fault protection trips
Symptom.description: Earth fault protection trips during start-up failure.

Symptom.name: unable to load the system software
Symptom.description: The system software cannot be loaded during start-up failure.

Symptom.name: FlexPendant not responding
Symptom.description: The FlexPendant is not responding during start-up failure.

Symptom.name: FlexPendant starts but does not respond to input
Symptom.description: The FlexPendant starts, but does not respond to any input.

Symptom.name: disk containing the system software does not start correctly
Symptom.description: The disk containing the system software does not start correctly.

Symptom.name: FlexPendant starts but does not communicate with the controller
Symptom.description: The FlexPendant starts but does not display a screen image. No entries are possible, and no functions are available.

Symptom.name: Controller LED indicators not lit
Symptom.description: LED indicators are not lit.

Symptom.name: Program execution is sluggish
Symptom.description: Program execution is sluggish, seemingly irrational and sometimes stalls.

Symptom.name: FlexPendant completely or intermittently dead
Symptom.description: The FlexPendant is completely or intermittently "dead". No entries are possible, and no functions are available.

Symptom.name: FlexPendant starts but does not display a screen image
Symptom.description: The FlexPendant starts but does not display a screen image. No entries are possible, and no functions are available.

Symptom.name: wrong input voltage to DSQC 604
Symptom.description: No or wrong input voltage is detected to DSQC 604.

Symptom.name: Status LED pulsing green on DSQC 662
Symptom.description: The Status LED on DSQC 662 is pulsing green, indicating a USB communication error.

Symptom.name: DSQC 662 Status LED red
Symptom.description: The indicator LED on DSQC 662 is red.

Symptom.name: Low controller performance
Symptom.description: The controller performance is low, and seems to work irrationally.

Symptom.name: System cannot be operated or started
Symptom.description: The system cannot be operated or started at all.

Symptom.name: Equipment connected to service outlet does not work
Symptom.description: Equipment connected to the Control Module service outlet does not work.

Symptom.name: Firmware reflashing process fails
Symptom.description: When reflashing firmware, the automatic process can fail.

Symptom.name: Mechanical noise
Symptom.description: During operation, mechanical noise is emitted from motors, gearboxes, bearings, or similar.

Symptom.name: Manipulator crashes on power down
Symptom.description: The manipulator works correctly while Motors ON is active, but when Motors OFF is active, it collapses under its own weight.

Symptom.name: DCOK LED off
Symptom.description: DCOK LED on DSQC 661 is off.

Symptom.description: Wrong DC level on DSQC 661.

Symptom.description: USB communication error.

CorrectiveAction.name: secure the robot arm system by other means
CorrectiveAction.description: Secure the robot arm system by other means before working on it if the holding brakes are suspected to be non-operational.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. If you suspect that the holding brakes are non-operational, secure the robot arm system by some other means before working on it.

CorrectiveAction.name: switch off incoming mains power supply
CorrectiveAction.description: Switch off the incoming mains power supply before opening the rear cover of either module.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the incoming mains power supply has been switched off.

CorrectiveAction.name: verify no voltage with voltmeter
CorrectiveAction.description: Use a voltmeter to verify that there is no voltage between any of the terminals.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Use a voltmeter to verify that there is not voltage between any of the terminals.

CorrectiveAction.name: use a wrist strap
CorrectiveAction.description: Use a wrist strap to prevent ESD damage.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Use a wrist strap.

CorrectiveAction.name: use an ESD protective floor mat
CorrectiveAction.description: Use an ESD protective floor mat grounded through a current-limiting resistor.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Use an ESD protective floor mat.

CorrectiveAction.name: use a dissipative table mat
CorrectiveAction.description: Use a dissipative table mat grounded to provide controlled discharge of static voltages.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Use a dissipative table mat.

CorrectiveAction.name: wait until the component has cooled
CorrectiveAction.description: Wait until the potentially hot component has cooled before removing or handling it.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Wait until the potentially hot component has cooled if it is to be removed or handled in any other way.

CorrectiveAction.name: remove left behind tools
CorrectiveAction.description: Remove all special tools left behind when maintenance work is complete.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure all such tools are removed when maintenance work is complete!

CorrectiveAction.name: Restore mains power supply within specifications
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure the main power supply to the system is present and within specified limits.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure the main power supply to the system is present and is within the specified limits.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect FlexPendant correctly to Control Module
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure the main transformer in the Drive module is correctly connected to the mains voltage levels at hand.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure that the main transformer in the Drive module is correctly connected to the mains voltage levels at hand.

CorrectiveAction.name: switch on main switches
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that the main switches are switched on.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure that the main switches are switched on.

CorrectiveAction.name: verify power supply to Control module and Drive module
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that the power supply to the Control module and Drive module are within specified limits.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure that the power supply to the Control module and Drive module are within the specified limits.

CorrectiveAction.name: Ensure mains power supply is working
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that the mains power supply is working and the voltage level matches that of the controller requirement.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Ensure that the mains power supply is working. 2. Ensure that the voltage level matches that of the controller requirement.

CorrectiveAction.name: Ensure main transformer is connected correctly
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that the main transformer is connected correctly to the mains voltage level.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Ensure that the main transformer is connected correctly to the mains voltage level.

CorrectiveAction.name: Ensure mains fuse Q1 is not tripped
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that the mains fuse Q1 inside the Drive Module is not tripped.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Ensure that the mains fuse (Q1) inside the Drive Module is not tripped.

CorrectiveAction.name: Ensure connections between Drive and Control modules are correct
CorrectiveAction.description: Ensure that all the connections between the Drive module and the Control module are connected correctly.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. If the Drive Module does not start although the Control Module is working and the Drive Module main switch has been switched on, ensure that all the connections between the Drive module and the Control module are connected correctly.

CorrectiveAction.name: Add short WAIT instructions
CorrectiveAction.description: Add one or more short WAIT instructions to avoid fast program loops.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: To avoid such loops, you can test by adding one or more WAIT instructions. Use only short WAIT times, to avoid slowing the program down unnecessarily.

CorrectiveAction.name: Adjust I/O update interval values
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the I/O update interval value for each I/O board is not too low.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the I/O update interval value for each I/O board is not too low. 2. Change these values using RobotStudio. 3. I/O units that are not read regularly may be switched to “change of state” operation as detailed in the RobotStudio manual.

CorrectiveAction.name: Program PLC with event driven instructions
CorrectiveAction.description: Change PLC programming to use event driven instructions instead of looped instructions.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Program the PLC in such a way that it uses event driven instructions, instead of looped instructions. 2. Use the fixed system inputs and outputs that may be used for this purpose.

CorrectiveAction.name: Switch on main switch
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the main switch has been switched on.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure the main switch has been switched on.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reconnect cables from power supply unit to main computer
CorrectiveAction.description: Check all cables from power supply unit to main computer, making sure these are correctly connected.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check all cables from power supply unit to main computer. 2. Make sure these are correctly connected.

CorrectiveAction.name: Check main transformer connection
CorrectiveAction.description: Check the main transformer connection and match terminal voltages to shop supply voltage.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check the main transformer connection. The voltages are marked on the terminals. Make sure they match the shop supply voltage.

CorrectiveAction.name: Close circuit breaker F6
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure circuit breaker F6 is closed in position 3.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure circuit breaker F6 (if used) is closed in position 3.

CorrectiveAction.name: Restore contactor K41 operation
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure contactor K41 opens and closes when ordered.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure contactor K41 opens and closes when ordered.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset earth fault protection condition
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the circuit breaker in the Control Module has not been tripped and connected equipment does not consume too much power.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure the circuit breaker in the Control Module has not been tripped. Make sure any equipment connected to the service outlet does not consume too much power, causing the circuit breaker to trip.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset earth fault protection F4 condition
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the earth fault protection has not been tripped and connected equipment does not conduct current to ground.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure the earth fault protection has not been tripped. Make sure any equipment connected to the service outlet does not conduct current to ground, causing the earth fault protection to trip.

CorrectiveAction.name: Restore power supply within specifications
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the power supply to the robot system is within specifications.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check USB connection on both ends. 2. Try to fix the communication between the power supply and the computer by reconnecting the cable. 3. Make sure that the USB cable is properly connected on both ends.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect transformer A correctly
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the transformer (A) supplying the outlet is correctly connected, i.e. input and output voltages in accordance with specifications.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the transformer (A) supplying the outlet is correctly connected, i.e. input and output voltages in accordance with specifications.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect FlexPendant correctly to controller
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the system is switched on and that the FlexPendant is connected to the controller.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check the cabling. 2. Make sure that the cabling is correctly connected and not faulty. 3. If the cabling is found unconnected or faulty, connect/replace it. 4. Verify that the fault has been fixed and restart this guide if necessary.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace FlexPendant if cable is faulty
CorrectiveAction.description: Inspect all cable insulation for damage. Replace any faulty cabling as detailed in the product manual for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Inspect all cable insulation for damage. 2. Replace any faulty cabling as detailed in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect cables from power supply unit to main computer correctly
CorrectiveAction.description: Check all cables from power supply unit to main computer and make sure they are correctly connected.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check all cables from power supply unit to main computer, making sure these are correctly connected.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect FlexPendant correctly to controller
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the FlexPendant has been correctly connected to the controller.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check connection between DC output and connected unit. 2. Make sure that the power supply is connected to DSQC 662. 3. If the connection is faulty or the power supply is not connected to DSQC 662, repair connection/connect it. 4. Verify that the fault has been fixed and restart this guide if necessary.

CorrectiveAction.name: Refit internal manipulator cabling
CorrectiveAction.description: Inspect all internal manipulator cabling, especially all cabling disconnected, connected re-routed or bundled during recent repair work. Refit any cabling as detailed in the product manual for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Inspect all internal manipulator cabling, especially all cabling disconnected, connected re-routed or bundled during recent repair work. 2. Refit any cabling as detailed in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace faulty cabling
CorrectiveAction.description: Inspect cable insulation for damage and replace faulty cabling.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Inspect all cable insulation for damage. Replace any faulty cabling as detailed in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Set controller to manual mode
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the controller is in manual mode.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Make sure the controller is in manual mode.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset the FlexPendant
CorrectiveAction.description: Reset the FlexPendant. Press Reset button located on the back of the FlexPendant.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Reset the FlexPendant. 2. Press Reset button located on the back of the FlexPendant.

CorrectiveAction.name: Recalibrate robot axes
CorrectiveAction.description: Recalibrate the robot axes if required.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check the revolution counters’ positions. 2. Update if required. 3. If required, recalibrate the robot axes.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace faulty motor or gearbox
CorrectiveAction.description: Locate the faulty bearing by tracking the noise and replace it.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Locate the faulty motor by tracking the noise. 2. Study the path of the robot TCP to establish which axis, and thus which motor, may be faulty. 3. Replace the faulty motor/gearbox as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace faulty motor or gearbox
CorrectiveAction.description: Locate the faulty motor by tracking the noise and replace the faulty motor or gearbox.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Locate the faulty motor by tracking the noise. Replace the faulty motor/gearbox as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace faulty parallel bar
CorrectiveAction.description: Check the trueness of the parallel bar and replace the faulty parallel bar.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check the trueness of the parallel bar (applies to robots fitted with parallel bars only). Replace the faulty parallel bar as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Connect correct robot type in configuration
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the correct robot type is connected as specified in the configuration files.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the correct robot type is connected as specified in the configuration files.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace seals and gaskets
CorrectiveAction.description: Inspect all seals and gaskets between motor and gearbox and replace them.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Observe the safety information in section CAUTION - Hot parts may cause burns! on page 21 before approaching the potentially hot robot component. 2. Inspect all seals and gaskets between motor and gearbox. 3. Replace seals and gaskets as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Correct gearbox oil level
CorrectiveAction.description: Check the gearbox oil level and correct it according to specification.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check the gearbox oil level. Correct oil level is specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Check recommended oil level and type
CorrectiveAction.description: Check the recommended oil level and type as specified in the product manual for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check the recommended oil level and type as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: secure all cabling and connectors
CorrectiveAction.description: Check all cabling and make sure connectors are connected securely.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check all the cabling, especially the cables in the Emergency stop and Enable chains. 2. Make sure all connectors are connected securely.

CorrectiveAction.name: adjust cabinet input voltage
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace DSQC 661 when the input voltage is correct and the unit may be faulty.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure that the input voltage to the cabinet is the correct one for that particular cabinet. 2. If the input voltage is incorrect, adjust it. 3. Verify that the fault has been fixed and restart this guide if necessary.

CorrectiveAction.name: check USB connection on both ends
CorrectiveAction.description: Check the USB connection on both ends for DSQC 662 communication issues.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Check USB connection on both ends.

CorrectiveAction.name: reconnect USB cable
CorrectiveAction.description: Reconnect the USB cable to restore communication between the power supply and the computer.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Try to fix the communication between the power supply and the computer by reconnecting the cable. Make sure that the USB cable is properly connected on both ends.

CorrectiveAction.name: troubleshoot DSQC 661
CorrectiveAction.description: Troubleshoot DSQC 661 when DSQC 662 input voltage is wrong.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: If no or the wrong input voltage is detected, troubleshoot DSQC 661.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace Drive Module power supply
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace the Drive Module power supply when incoming voltage is correct but LEDs still do not work.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Disconnect connector X1 from the Drive Module power supply and measure the incoming voltage. 2. Measure between pins X1.1 and X1.5. 3. If the power supply incoming voltage is correct (230 VAC) but the LEDs still do not work, replace the Drive Module power supply. 4. Replace the power supply as detailed in the product manual for the controller.

CorrectiveAction.name: Use identical RobotWare versions
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the versions of the old and new unit is identical.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Was the relevant unit recently replaced? 2. If YES; make sure the versions of the old and new unit is identical.

CorrectiveAction.name: Correct tool and work object definition
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the robot tool and work object are correctly defined.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the robot tool and work object are correctly defined.

CorrectiveAction.name: Restore brake operation
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the robot brakes work properly.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the robot brakes work properly. 2. Proceed as detailed in section Problem releasing Robot brakes on page 50.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace complete motor
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace faulty motors as a complete unit.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Bearings inside motors are not to be replaced individually. 2. Replace the complete motor as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Fit bearings correctly
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the bearings are fitted correctly.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Make sure the bearings are fitted correctly. 2. Also see the product manual for the robot for general instruction on how to handle bearings.

CorrectiveAction.name: Ensure sufficient bearing lubrication
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the bearing has sufficient lubrication.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Determine which bearing is emitting the noise. 2. Make sure the bearing has sufficient lubrication as specified in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace motor as complete unit after oil leak inspection
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace the motor as a complete unit if the motor is found faulty after resolver inspection.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Remove the resolver of the motor to see if there are any signs of oil leaks. 2. If found faulty, replace the motor as a complete unit as detailed in the product manual for the robot.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace DSQC 661
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace DSQC 661 when a short circuit is found on DSQC 661 or when the unit may be faulty.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. The 661 may be faulty, replace it and verify that the fault has been fixed.

CorrectiveAction.name: Open fuse F2 or F6
CorrectiveAction.description: Open main fuse F2 and optional fuse F6 if used when they are closed.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check main fuse F2 and optional fuse F6 if used. 2. If the fuses are closed, open them. 3. Verify that the fault has been fixed and restart this guide if necessary.

CorrectiveAction.name: Fix short circuit
CorrectiveAction.description: Correct short circuit on DSQC 661 output.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Fix short circuit.
